label: prop:torus-knot-delta-q-writhe
title: Writhe exponent of the torus-knot $\delta_q$ decoration: $\delta_q(T_{m,p}) = h\,[(m-1)p]_q$
html:
For the torus knot T_{m,p} presented on the minimal number of strands — that is, with m \leq p, so that m is the braid index (Morton–Williams; see the box-braid irreducibility proof) — the \delta_q-decoration extracts the quantum integer at the writhe w = (m-1)p:

  \delta_q(T_{m,p}) \;=\; q^{w} - q^{-w} \;=\; h\,[w]_q.

The decoration corresponds to the bar-odd part of the top-channel twist. The writhe exponent governs the h\,[w]_q form across all torus knots, cleanly matching the 10_{124} = T_{3,5} and 8_{19} = T_{3,4} force-carrier evaluations.

The minimal-strand condition is not cosmetic. T_{m,p} \cong T_{p,m} as knots, but (m-1)p \neq (p-1)m whenever m \neq p: the trefoil read as T_{2,3} gives w = 3 and read as T_{3,2} gives w = 4; 10_{124} gives 10 or 12. Without the condition the statement would assign two different \delta_q to the same knot. This is the general fact that the writhe is not a link invariant (QOU/StandardModel/WritheMarkovInvariance.lean), specialised to the torus family. Fixing the braid index is exactly the framework's "evaluate at the lowest level of the tower", and the compute already presents every force carrier with m < p, so no evaluated number changes. As a consistency check, (w - m) \bmod 2 — the level-pair invariant of QOU/StandardModel/WritheLevelParity.lean — agrees across both presentations of each carrier, while w alone does not.
